title: Escalation result
description: findings/<finding_id>/escalate.json. Proves real impact from a realistic in-scope attacker position, or honestly reports that it could not.

verdict.description: ESCALATED = a higher impact was actually executed. AS_FOUND = the original impact stands, nothing further reached. NOT_ESCALATABLE = the finding does not survive contact with a realistic attacker position.

citation.description: The specific policy/scope line relied on. 'I assume it's in scope' is not a citation.

privileges_held.description: Every privilege the attacker needs, named exactly. A privilege quietly assumed away here is the single most common cause of an Informative closure.

requires_admin_trust.description: True if the exploit needs the attacker to already be an admin-configured trusted entity (allowlist entry, preconfigured connector). Findings of this shape have been triaged Informational regardless of technical quality.

executed.description: False means it was reasoned about, not run. Escalations that were not executed do not count as escalations.

ceiling_reason.description: Why no higher impact was reached — the boundary that actually stopped it.

not_attempted.description: Escalations deliberately not attempted because they would be unsafe, destructive, or out of scope.

poc_steps.description: Ordered, self-contained. verifier reproduces from these alone and never sees this file's reasoning.

calibration_checked.description: Which memory/general-lessons.md lessons (always applicable) and which memory/closed-reports/<target>/ entries were read. An empty target corpus is expected on a new target; the general lessons are still required.
